relationships.subject: Angeli's salt
relationships.evidence_quote: Angeli's salt solution (AS, 300 µM) caused short-lasting vigorous increases in neuronal activity of primary meningeal afferents, followed by deactivation and desensitisation.

relationships.subject: Nitroxyl
relationships.evidence_quote: has previously been shown to release the vasodilator neuropeptide CGRP from primary meningeal afferents and to thus increase meningeal blood flow in rodents

relationships.subject: Acrolein
relationships.evidence_quote: the mechanically evoked activity was reduced after acrolein application

relationships.subject: TRPA1
relationships.evidence_quote: there is evidence that TRPA1 activation may have an inhibitory function in the nociceptive trigeminal system

key_findings: Angeli's salt briefly activates then long-lastingly deactivates meningeal afferents, independent of TRPA1 and TRPV1 (effects persisted or were stronger in knockouts).
Acrolein reduced mechanically evoked spinal trigeminal activity; no evidence that TRPA1 activation triggers headache.
